claims.text: The proposed intervention is a minor copper addition to AlCoCrFeNi followed by homogenization.
Adding a minor amount of copper to AlCoCrFeNi will enhance its heat-transfer capability.
Copper-modified AlCoCrFeNi will maintain structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi can be produced by plasma arc additive manufacturing.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi alloy has established mechanical properties but only moderate thermal conductivity.
Arc melting followed by thorough homogenization will produce a uniform dispersion of copper in AlCoCrFeNi.
Uniformly dispersed copper will refine the microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi.
Homogeneously distributed copper will help maintain phase stability in the AlCoCrFeNi matrix.
Copper has high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Copper addition will enhance phonon-mediated heat transfer in the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Uniform copper distribution will minimize local compositional inhomogeneities.
Minimizing local compositional inhomogeneities will preserve mechanical integrity during thermal cycling and mechanical loading.
The copper-alloyed material will have significantly higher thermal conductivity than copper-free AlCoCrFeNi.
The copper-alloyed material will retain mechanical strength comparable to copper-free AlCoCrFeNi.
The copper-alloyed material will retain microstructural stability under the specified high-temperature cyclic-loading conditions.
Standard AlCoCrFeNi is currently used as an intermediate material and has limited heat-transfer capability.
The predicted improvement should occur at approximately 700°C under cyclic mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing reactor environments.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as plasma-arc additively manufactured, whereas the intervention and both experimental groups are described as arc-melted and homogenized. This changes the baseline processing route and prevents a direct comparison to the stated initial material unless the relationship between the two routes is clarified.
